audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 15, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal genealogical, textual, and political audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for idealized David memory, Maacah's queen-mother role, qadesh translation, religious reform, temple treasury diplomacy, siege and proxy war, compulsory labor, foot disease, assassination, dynastic massacre, and prophetic-fulfillment claims.

verses.restored: In eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
He walked in all sins his father did before him, and his heart was not whole with YHWH his Divine like heart of David his ancestor.
Nevertheless, for David's sake YHWH his Divine gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising his son after him and establishing Jerusalem.
For David did upright in eyes of YHWH and did not turn aside from anything commanded all days of his life, except in matter of Uriah the Hittite.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all days of his life.
Rest of acts of Abijam and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam lay with his ancestors, and they buried him in City of David. Asa his son reigned in his place.
In twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign over Judah.
He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother/queen mother was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did upright in eyes of YHWH like David his ancestor.
He removed male cult personnel/consecrated persons from land and removed all idols his ancestors made.
He also removed Maacah his mother/queen mother from being queen mother because she made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it at wadi Kidron.
But high places were not removed. Nevertheless Asa's heart was whole with YHWH all his days.
He brought into house of YHWH things his father dedicated and things he dedicated: silver, gold, and vessels.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

Asa took all silver and gold remaining in treasures of house of YHWH and king's house and placed them in hand of his servants. King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram living in Damascus, saying:
There is covenant between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I sent you a gift of silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so he will go up from me.
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent commanders of armies against cities of Israel. He struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, all Chinneroth, and all land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard, he stopped building Ramah and lived in Tirzah.
King Asa summoned all Judah; none was exempt. They carried stones of Ramah and timber with which Baasha built, and King Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
Rest of all acts of Asa, all his might, all he did, and cities he built—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah? Yet in time of his old age he became diseased in his feet.
Asa lay with his ancestors and was buried with them in City of David his ancestor. Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
Nadab son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in second year of Asa king of Judah and reigned over Israel two years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH and walked in way of his father and his sin by which he made Israel sin.
Baasha son of Ahijah, from house of Issachar, conspired against him. Baasha struck him at Gibbethon belonging to Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.
In third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha killed him and reigned in his place.
When he reigned, he struck all house of Jeroboam. He did not leave to Jeroboam any breathing being until he destroyed him, according to word of YHWH spoken by servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
because of sins Jeroboam sinned and made Israel sin, by provocation with which he provoked YHWH, Divine of Israel.
Rest of acts of Nadab and all he did—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah began to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty-four years.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH and walked in way of Jeroboam and his sin by which he made Israel sin.

translation_notes: The summary that David never turned aside except in the matter of Uriah is royal idealization. The wider narrative records Bathsheba's coercion, census deaths, imperial violence, and household failures that must not be erased.

Maacah's precise genealogy and whether she is Asa's mother or grandmother/queen mother require audit. Her removal from office is political and religious action, not permission for misogyny or violence against older women.
Verse 12 again uses qadesh. It must not be translated or weaponized as a condemnation of LGBTQ identity; the historical reference is likely cultic personnel.
Religious reform does not authorize persecution, destruction of living communities' sacred property, forced conversion, or punishment of private belief.
Asa empties temple and palace treasuries to purchase Ben-hadad's betrayal of Baasha. Sacred wealth funds a proxy invasion whose victims live in northern cities.
Baasha's Ramah blockade restricts movement and economic life. Asa answers with foreign attack and then conscripts all Judah, with no exemption, to move construction materials.
Asa's foot disease in old age is a medical condition, not evidence of moral or spiritual failure.
Baasha's assassination of Nadab during siege and extermination of Jeroboam's entire house are coup violence and dynastic massacre. Prophetic fulfillment does not make collective killing ethical.
The narrative repeatedly says war continued all their days; ordinary communities bear the prolonged cost behind short royal summaries.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter against LGBTQ people, older women, disabled or ill people, or religious minorities. Do not sanctify proxy war, compulsory labor, assassination, or dynastic massacre through reform, prophecy, or idealized royal memory.
